Title: Collaborating with Generative AI in Consumer Culture Research
Why It Matters: Strongest anchor available: JCR (top-3 marketing journal, the home journal for qualitative/consumer-culture work specifically) publishing directly on how to integrate GenAI into qualitative/textual consumer research, interview-based practices and principles. More on-point than Arora et al. for a qualitative-methods defense - cite both, lead with this one.

Authors: Arora, N., Chakraborty, I., & Nishimura, Y.
Title: AI-Human Hybrids for Marketing Research: Leveraging LLMs as Collaborators
Why It Matters: Load-bearing citation. Top-5 marketing journal; finds human+LLM hybrid coding matches/exceeds human-only on theme generation. This is the exact claim reviewers need to accept.

Title: Everyday Activism: An AI-Assisted Netnography of a Digital Consumer Movement
Why It Matters: Kozinets basically invented netnography - a marketing-journal AI-assisted qualitative study by the field's own authority. Strong precedent if either paper uses digital/social consumer text data.

Authors: Herhausen, D., Ludwig, S., Abedin, E., Ul Haque, N., & de Jong, D.
Title: From Words to Insights: Text Analysis in Business Research
Why It Matters: Strong general-purpose citation: JBR framework paper comparing topic models/dictionaries/supervised ML/LLMs for business text data, with explicit guidelines for authors and reviewers on method selection and evaluation. Useful to cite for why LLM-based text analysis is a legitimate, reviewer-recognized method choice in business research generally, not just qualitative coding specifically.

Title: Sports

Authors: Pueschel, J., Hao, S., & Schmitt, B.
Title: Understanding Luxury Shaming: A Multi-Study Exploration Using Qualitative Inquiry and Generative AI
Why It Matters: Applied precedent in the same journal family (JBR) explicitly integrating traditional qualitative technique with GenAI analysis on a consumer-behavior topic - close methodological cousin to the Tariff/CCS/Data Center papers' own Study 1 design.

Title: From Code Variability to Theme Convergence: AI-Human Alignment in Thematic Analysis With Claude Code
Why It Matters: Only paper validating Claude Code specifically (not just chat-based Claude) against a human/NVivo baseline. Directly defends the tool choice, not just 'an LLM.' NOT on jump drive - worth adding.

Authors: Misra, R., Dahal, R., Kirk, B., Khan, R., Dogan, G., Chataut, R., & Gyawali, P.
Title: Large Language Models in Qualitative Analysis: Comparing Traditional and Researcher-Interpreted Approaches
Why It Matters: Comparative study of traditional vs. researcher-interpreted LLM analysis approaches - reliability evidence.

Why It Matters: Introduces GAITA (Guided AI Thematic Analysis), adapting King et al.'s Template Analysis with researcher as reflexive instrument guiding GPT-4 through 4 stages. Also the paper most likely to be cited AGAINST you (raises the Big-Q/reflexivity objection) - read both ways.

Authors: Sakaguchi, K., Sakama, R., & Watari, T.

Title: Risky or Rigorous? Developing Trustworthiness Criteria for AI-Supported Qualitative Data Analysis
Why It Matters: Proposes trustworthiness criteria (credibility, dependability, confirmability, transferability) adapted for AI-assisted analysis. Gives a rigor framework to cite in the methods section. NOT on jump drive - worth adding.

Title: Doing Thematic Analysis in the Age of Generative AI: Practices
Why It Matters: https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/16094069261425173
column10: Directly engages the reflexivity/Big-Q objection; models how to write a methods section that keeps human interpretive authority visible.

Title: AI-Augmented Netnography: Ethical and Methodological Frameworks for Responsible Digital Research
Why It Matters: Ethical/methodological framework specifically for AI-augmented netnography - pairs well with the Kozinets paper if either project uses digital consumer data.

Title: Human-AI Collaborative Inductive Thematic Analysis: AI Guided Analysis and Human Interpretive Authority
Why It Matters: Frames Claude Code as assistant-with-human-final-authority - the safest positioning for reviewers. NOT on jump drive.

Authors: Paulus, T., Lester, J.N., & Davis, C.
Title: The Construction of the Role of AI in Qualitative Data Analysis in the Social Sciences
Why It Matters: Discourse analysis of 29 published articles' own framing of AI's role in QDA, identifying 5 stances researchers take (from 'QDA is inherently problematic' to 'AI-human hybrid is the future' to 'automation is inevitable'). Directly useful for choosing defensible methods-section language: shows which framing stance ('AI-human hybrid methods are the future') is the safest and most established one to write into, rather than guessing at the right rhetorical posture.

Title: (same paper as above - Tier 2 entry)
Why It Matters: Represents the Braun & Clarke 'Big Q' objection - reflexive TA's point is researcher subjectivity, and AI 'systematic/reduce-bias' framing is methodologically incongruent. A reviewer trained in reflexive TA may raise exactly this - address head-on in methods, don't get blindsided.

Title: To Vibe Research or Not to Vibe Research? Generative AI in Qualitative Research
Why It Matters: Skeptical framing - useful for anticipating reviewer language and objections. NOT on jump drive.

Title: Thematic Analysis and Artificial Intelligence: A Step-by-Step Process for Using ChatGPT in Thematic Analysis
Why It Matters: Maps AI onto Braun & Clarke's six-phase process step by step - probably the single best template for writing an actual methods section paragraph.
